title: The Jetson ONE costs $128,000 and it can carry you above city traffic
title_candidates: The Jetson ONE costs $128,000 and it can carry you above city traffic
How the Jetson ONE lifts one person off the ground with no runway
The Jetson ONE was built to replace the part of your commute stuck in traffic
A Swedish startup built the Jetson ONE, a $128,000 one-person flying machine
The Jetson ONE is a personal aircraft with almost no flight training required
caption:
The Jetson ONE is a one-person electric aircraft designed to take off and land almost anywhere, no runway or airport needed. It sells for $128,000.

Most of the flying is handled by the aircraft's own software, which keeps it stable automatically. The person on board chooses a direction and the machine does the rest. That is a significant change from traditional aircraft, which require years of training before you can legally leave the ground.

Whether personal air vehicles like this one become part of daily life depends on how fast the price falls and how cities decide to handle traffic at low altitude.
